title: 08. Files & Errors: STRUCT, ARRAY & BINARY DATA
summary: STRUCT, ARRAY & BINARY DATA: STRUCT — Pack/Unpack Binary Data; Used for: network protocols, file formats, C struct interop.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/binary_data.py
import struct
import array

# ============================================================
# STRUCT — Pack/Unpack Binary Data
# ============================================================
# Used for: network protocols, file formats, C struct interop

# Pack Python values into bytes
packed = struct.pack(">I2sf", 1, b"AB", 3.14)
# > = big-endian, I = unsigned int, 2s = 2-char string, f = float
print(packed)  # b'\x00\x00\x00\x01AB@H\xf5\xc3'

# Unpack bytes into Python values
unpacked = struct.unpack(">I2sf", packed)
print(unpacked)  # (1, b'AB', 3.140000104904175)

# Format characters:
# b=int8, B=uint8, h=int16, H=uint16, i=int32, I=uint32
# q=int64, Q=uint64, f=float32, d=float64, s=char[], ?=bool
# < little-endian, > big-endian, ! network (big-endian)

# Practical: Parse a simple binary file header
def parse_header(data: bytes) -> dict:
    magic, version, num_records = struct.unpack_from(">4sHI", data)
    return {
        "magic": magic.decode(),
        "version": version,
        "num_records": num_records,
    }

# ============================================================
# ARRAY — Efficient numeric arrays (like C arrays)
# ============================================================
# More memory-efficient than lists for numeric data

arr = array.array("i", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])  # Signed int array
print(arr[0])          # 1
arr.append(6)
arr.extend([7, 8, 9])

# Type codes: b=int8, B=uint8, i=int32, I=uint32, f=float32, d=float64

# To/from bytes
binary = arr.tobytes()
arr2 = array.array("i")
arr2.frombytes(binary)

# Memory comparison
import sys
lst = list(range(1000))
arr = array.array("i", range(1000))
print(f"List: {sys.getsizeof(lst)} bytes")   # ~8056 bytes
print(f"Array: {sys.getsizeof(arr)} bytes")  # ~4064 bytes (half!)

# ============================================================
# MEMORYVIEW — Zero-copy buffer access
# ============================================================
data = bytearray(b"Hello, World!")
view = memoryview(data)

# Slice without copying!
sub = view[7:12]
sub[:] = b"Earth"
print(data)  # bytearray(b'Hello, Earth!')
```
